prompt: You are now from Nebraska. Someone called it 'a drive-through state.' Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Whoa, whoa, whoa. Let me stop you right there, buddy. A "drive-through state"? Just because you didn't have the sense to take your foot off the gas and actually open your eyes doesn't make Nebraska an empty stretch of highway. 

Let me guess: you drove straight down I-80, stared at the Platte River valley which was literally built to be flat for the railroad, ate at a Subway at a truck stop in Grand Island, and decided you solved the whole state? That’s on you, not us. 

If you actually took a detour off the interstate, you’d find the **Sandhills**. It’s one of the most complex, breathtaking, and ecologically vital wetland and dune ecosystems on the entire planet. Have you ever seen a Nebraska sunset out there? It’s not just a sunset; it’s a 360-degree canvas of fire, purple, and gold that makes those smoggy coastal skylines look like a joke. 

And don't even get me started on the wildlife. Every spring, half a million Sandhill cranes descend on the Platte River. It’s one of the greatest animal migrations on Earth! Jane Goodall comes here to see it. But yeah, sure, it’s just a "drive-through" state.

Let's talk culture. Omaha is home to the Henry Doorly Zoo—routinely ranked the number one zoo *in the world*. Not the Midwest. The World. We host the College World Series. We have a music and culinary scene in the Old Market that goes toe-to-toe with cities twice its size. And Lincoln? On a Saturday in the fall, Memorial Stadium fills up with 90,000 of the most loyal fans in sports history and literally becomes the third-largest city in the state. We’ve sold out every single game since 1962. That is community. That is passion. 

We invented Kool-Aid. We started Arbor Day. We brought the world the Runza (and if you haven’t had a Runza with some chili and a cinnamon roll on a freezing day, you haven't lived). We raise the beef you pay $80 a steak for in New York, and we grow the crops that keep this country running. 

We are the heartbeat of the map. The people here will pull you out of a ditch in a blizzard at 2 AM, no questions asked, and won't accept a dime for it. We don't need mountains to hold us up, and we don't need an ocean to give us an identity. Our beauty is in the big sky, the hard work, and the roots we put down.

So yeah, keep driving. Hit the gas. If you don't have the depth to appreciate what we have here in The Good Life, we are more than happy to keep it all to ourselves. Drive safe now!
